knowledge.text: The edit broadens the Search Efficiency guidance from multi-instance-only to all unmet tasks (including single-object "put a clean <object> in <receptacle>" and transform-and-place tasks) and adds cycle-breaking: when recent actions cycle among the same small set of locations without acquiring the exact target, choose an admissible candidate with a different location or type. In val:0010 ("cool some apple and put it in microwave"), the candidate did not apply this: while not yet holding the apple it repeatedly cycled through countertop1, cabinet1, countertop2, and fridge (Q10:3–Q10:12), only then went to diningtable1 at Q10:13, took the apple at Q10:14, and finished in 19 steps; the parent reached diningtable1 earlier (P10:9) and finished in 15 steps. Both succeeded, so this is an efficiency/behavior counterexample rather than a failure, and it shows the cycle-breaking clause was not followed despite repeated revisits of the same locations.

Broadened coverage guidance (when recent checks are mostly one container type, prefer a different admissible container/surface type such as a cabinet, shelf, basin, countertop, or diningtable) is consistent with one single-object improvement: in val:0004 ("put a mug in sidetable"), with no mug visible at the start, the candidate went directly to diningtable1, took mug1, and placed it on sidetable1 in 4 steps, while the parent searched drawers 1–4 and both sidetables before finding a mug and finished in 12 steps; both succeeded. Because which unsearched location is tried first is a stochastic search choice the clause does not determine, this supports coverage being beneficial but does not isolate the clause's causal contribution.

The edit's instruction to stop searching once the exact target is held was not applied in a single-object examine-with task: in val:0001 ("examine the bowl with the desklamp"), the candidate held bowl1 at Q1:2 but then examined it (Q1:3) and visited shelf1 (Q1:4, which showed only pen1/pencil1) before returning to desk1 and reaching desklamp1 on dresser1, finishing in 7 steps, whereas the parent went from taking the bowl (P1:2) directly to dresser1 and used desklamp1 in 4 steps. Both succeeded; the candidate's extra steps show the stop-searching guidance did not prevent a held-target search detour (the clause names cleaning/transformation/placement specifically, so its applicability to an examine-with lamp task is limited).

The search/efficiency and Exact Object Type additions preserved prior capabilities where behavior was unchanged: in val:0006 ("put a clean butterknife in drawer") P6/Q6 were identical 8-step successes taking butterknife1 from countertop2, cleaning it at sinkbasin1, and moving it to drawer1; in val:0009 ("put a clean soapbar in toilet") P9/Q9 were identical 7-step successes taking soapbar1 from countertop1, cleaning it at sinkbasin1, and moving it to toilet1; val:0002 ("examine the pillow with the desklamp"), val:0003 ("put some mug on sidetable"), and val:0005 ("put some pencil on desk") were also identical-step successes (5, 4, and 5 steps). These identical pairs show no regression but do not test the edit's new search or exact-type clauses.

The new Exact Object Type clause (take only the exact task-named object, e.g., not a knife where a butterknife is required; resume searching instead of repeating a wrong-type placement) has limited current bearing: in val:0007 ("clean some butterknife and put it in drawer"), the parent took the wrong-type knife1 from drawer1 (P7:5), cleaned it at sinkbasin1 (P7:7), and moved it to drawer1 (P7:9), yet still hit the 50-step limit; the candidate saw the same knife1 in drawer1 (Q7:4) but never took it and also hit the 50-step limit. This is consistent with the clause discouraging wrong-type acquisition, but with both sides failing it gives no evidence the clause improves success, and the candidate's non-acquisition could equally reflect its own search choices.

Under the expanded coverage/anti-revisit guidance, the two current tasks that reached the 50-step limit never acquired the target or completed: in val:0008 ("put a clean soapbar in cabinet"), both sides failed while the candidate opened cabinets 1–4 and then repeatedly revisited them plus countertop1/sinkbasin1 (e.g., Q8:8–Q8:50) without ever taking a soapbar, and in val:0007 both sides also failed. This shows the guidance did not guarantee coverage of a target-containing location or stop revisiting under applicable conditions; the soapbar's location (or absence) is not established, so no global-absence conclusion follows.
